Since switching my work laptop from Wi-Fi to Ethernet, Microsoft Teams calls freeze for 3-5 seconds every few minutes even though normal web browsing seems fine. Please diagnose this from the details below and give me a step-by-step troubleshooting plan in priority order, with the most likely root causes first. I want fixes that minimize cost and avoid unnecessary hardware purchases. System: Dell Latitude 7420, Windows 11 Pro 23H2, Intel I219-LM Ethernet adapter, TP-Link Archer AX55 router, 300/300 Mbps fiber. Symptoms: during freezes, ping to 192.168.0.1 is usually 1 ms but occasionally spikes to 180-250 ms; Event Viewer repeatedly shows 'e2fexpress: Network link is disconnected' followed by reconnection; Device Manager still has 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power' enabled for the Ethernet adapter; the Ethernet cable is Cat5e, about 15 meters long, and runs next to a power strip and monitor cables. Already tried: rebooting the laptop and router, signing out of Teams, reinstalling Teams, and lowering call video quality. Please include: 1) likely causes ranked by probability, 2) exact Windows settings to change, 3) physical cable/router checks to try, 4) how to tell whether the issue is the cable, the NIC driver, power management, or the router port, and 5) a simple decision tree for what to test first, second, and third.

For a school board memo, synthesize the evidence from these five tutoring studies and recommend the best math-intervention option for a district serving grades 6-8. District context: 15 schools, 6000 students, 70% low-income, budget cap USD 1500 per participating student for the 2026-2027 school year, limited certified-teacher availability, preference for in-school delivery over after-school, and the superintendent wants measurable gains within one academic year.

Studies:
A) RCT, urban US, 2021-2022, n=1200 low-income students, daily 1:2 in-school tutoring by trained tutors; math +0.28 SD, attendance +3 percentage points, cost USD 3200/student/year.
B) Quasi-experimental, rural US, 2020-2021, n=800 students, weekly online tutoring; math +0.07 SD, attrition 25%, cost USD 900/student/year.
C) RCT, suburban US, 2019-2020, n=600 students, after-school small-group tutoring 2x/week; math +0.14 SD, no reading gains, cost USD 1400/student/year.
D) Pre-post single-group study, urban summer program, 2022, n=250 students, 4-week intensive tutoring; math +0.18 SD immediately after program but effects faded by midyear, cost USD 1100/student.
E) RCT, urban US, 2021-2022, n=450 students, in-school tutoring 3x/week led by paraprofessionals; math +0.11 SD overall and +0.19 SD for bottom-quartile students, cost USD 1000/student/year.

Please produce: (1) a study-quality ranking with brief justification, (2) a cost-effectiveness comparison using effect size per USD 1000, (3) the most defensible recommendation for this district, including whether to target all struggling students or only the bottom quartile, (4) the top 5 risks or threats to validity or external validity, (5) a 90-day pilot design with success metrics, sample-selection plan, and a go or no-go decision rule, and (6) a short executive summary in plain language for non-technical board members. Be explicit about assumptions and do not cite anything outside the information above.

Our physiotherapy clinic just switched to a new appointment-reminder workflow. Write a clear internal SOP for front-desk staff using the facts below. The document should include: purpose, scope, staff roles, required tools, step-by-step procedure, exception handling, quality-control checklist, and a short FAQ. Audience: nontechnical staff. Tone: professional, plain English. Length: 700-900 words. Use headings and bullets where useful.

Clinic facts:
- Clinic name: Riverbend Physio, Toronto, Canada.
- Staff roles: receptionist, therapist, clinic manager.
- Tools: booking calendar, SMS sender, email sender, spreadsheet log.
- Standard reminder schedule: send SMS 48 hours before each appointment at 10:00 America/Toronto; if no mobile number is available, send email instead; send a final SMS 3 hours before the appointment only for first-time patients.
- Message content must include: patient first name, appointment date and time, therapist name, clinic phone number, and cancellation policy.
- Cancellation policy: changes or cancellations require at least 24 hours' notice or a CAD 40 fee may apply.
- Consent rule: only send SMS if the patient has opted in; otherwise use email.
- Failed delivery rule: if both SMS and email fail, call once during business hours and log the outcome.
- Business hours: Monday-Friday 08:00-18:00, Saturday 09:00-14:00, closed Sunday.
- Logging fields: patient name, appointment datetime, channel used, sent time, delivery status, staff initials, notes.
- Exceptions: same-day bookings get only one reminder immediately after booking; recurring weekly appointments still follow the 48-hour rule; minors require the parent or guardian contact on file.
